title: Govee BLE device registry
description: Machine-readable registry of Govee BLE device families and their GATT/command surface, companion to docs/GOVEE_BLE_GATT_PROTOCOL.md.

source_app.description: APK the data was extracted from, e.g. 'com.govee.home 7.5.12 (1088)'.

hex_note.description: All byte values in this file are written as hex strings like '0x33' unless stated otherwise.

secret.description: Per-device authorization secret of secret_key_pairing families (0xB1/0xB2), not the AES cipher key.

scenes.description: Scene upload/activation model: the 0xA3 dialects, placeholders, cloud scene library and the AA 05 15 kelvin read-back.

mode_color_decode.description: Colour mode-report body decodes, keyed by govee_common::color_decode member (not_decoded aside), one per distinct layout, Kelvin signedness and CCT rule.

mode_color_parse.description: Colour-report strategies by name, each mapping colour sub-modes (0x15 / 0x0d / 0x0b / 0x02) to a mode_color_decode kind; an unlisted sub-mode is not decoded.

command_catalog.description: Shared command opcodes (BleProtocolConstants); per-family ones live in family.opcodes.

families.description: One entry per protocol family (a family may serve many SKUs).

hexByte.description: A single byte as a hex string, e.g. '0x33'.

confidence.description: high = controllers/SubMode classes read directly; medium = extracted by survey; low = inferred.

transport.description: Defaults shared by all families unless a family overrides them.

id.description: Stable family id, usually the pact/package name (e.g. 'h60ax').

models.description: SKU model numbers this family serves, e.g. ['H60A6','H1250'].

goods_types.description: Govee goodsType/pactCode integer ids, when known; a record with a non-zero goodsType routes to a family by goodsType alone, by SKU only when it is 0 (base-classes3/com/govee/kt/ui/device/SubConfig.java:46-62).

assigned_goods_type.description: goodsTypes the app assigns some of the family's SKUs itself: a matching device_list item (SKU in models, record goodsType in from_goods_type, condition holds) makes goods_type the gt that keys every control-screen goodsType lookup.

delivery.description: Whether the family ships in base.apk or as an on-demand pact_* split (base2home/pfd/Config).

gatt.description: Only present when the family overrides transport defaults.

multi_dialects.description: Multi-packet dialects used (0xA1 MultiPackageManager, 0xA3 MultipleControllerCommV1, 0xAC single-read/multi-reply).

submodes.description: Sub-mode type byte (the byte after mode command 0x05) per function; absent = unsupported.

opcodes.description: Device-specific command opcodes beyond the shared catalog.

pro_type.description: Header byte if not the default write 0x33 (hex, or a note when unresolved).

applies_to.description: Comma-separated SKUs the opcode is limited to (e.g. 'H5121, H5129'); absent = whole family.

segments.description: Segment/IC count, or a note when SKU-dependent.

kelvin_range.description: [min, max] CCT in kelvin, family-wide; a client_profile.by_goods_type row's kelvin_range, then the SKU's by_model kelvin_range, wins over it.

brightness_range.description: [min, max] on the wire (before any scaling), family-wide; a client_profile.by_goods_type row's brightness_range, then the SKU's by_model brightness_range, wins over it; [1, 100] = percent.

scene_versions.description: The control screen's ScenesConfigBean c (opScenesSet): the op set its scene list is filtered by (devices.yaml scenes.list_filter) and, where the bean has no apply set e (supportApplyOpSet), the versionArray parseSceneV1 uploads with (ScenesConfigBean.j: e, else c; sceneType -> comType, protocol §4.4); empty = a null c (no filter, activate only). Family-wide; a client_profile.by_goods_type row's scene_versions wins over it. Of the scene rows only H6052's bean has an e that differs (its row's doc).

notify.description: Inbound notify sub-types (byte after 0xEE) this family emits.

pact.description: Notes on the family's pact gates; a routed goodsType's accepted pacts are its client_profile.by_goods_type row's pacts.

name_prefixes.description: Advertised BLE name prefixes that resolve to this family (e.g. 'ihoment_H6047').

client_profile.description: Discriminators a thin client feeds the parametric .ksy types (facts not in the byte stream); wire is the govee_profile context as data.

has_brightness.description: Per-segment 0xA5 colour read-back record: true = 4-byte [brightness,R,G,B], false = 3-byte [R,G,B] (an aa a2 colour group is always 3-byte).

color_scheme.description: Colour-write byte-layout family, the app's colour instruction for the SKU (Config.J[version]): 'h60a6' = 0x15 with a segment mask (Bytes.h / Bytes.r), 'h6006' = 0x0d with the tint in both slots (Config.bu, Bytes.f / Bytes.p), 'h6188' = 0x0d with the white-slot CCT (Config.GM -> Bytes.A, the illumination tab's), 'h61a8' = 0x0b with no CCT (Config.cu, Bytes.d), 'h6061' = 0x15 colour version 5, whole device (Config.Zt: Bytes.l RGB, Bytes.u CCT), 'legacy_02' = 0x02, whole device (Config.fu: Bytes.a, and Bytes.o for a pick that is a Kelvin tint in the row's kelvin_range, which a row with rgb needs even without color_temp), 'kelvin_v9' = 15 04 <K u16be>, colour instruction 9, a Kelvin only: no RGB frame and no mask (Config.N[9] = JM -> Bytes.D; the colour page's Config.J[9] = hu maps a pick to its Kelvin first), 'h3010' = colour version 8, whole device (Config.gu: Bytes.j RGB, Bytes.t CCT), sent as one MultiController unit, the 0xA3 packets of govee_upload color_multi_value on comm byte 0x6e and then 33 05 15 00 (ColorModeControllerConfig.j, where LightColorCapabilityCenter.b2 holds: goodsType 411).

power_read.description: Power source (govee_state power_state.is_on): 'aa01' = the aa 01 read at connect, on when the byte == 1 (any non-zero byte under the wire power light_nonzero); 'ac_status' = TLV 0x01 of the 0xAC/0x03 status burst (no aa 01 read), on when the byte != 0; 'aa34_detail' = the aa 34 device-detail read at connect (no aa 01 read; wire f_34 device_detail), on when the header main switch shows on (govee_state device_detail.main_switch_on: the light open or white noise playing; H6057); 'advert' = no GATT read: only the advertisement's switch byte, read as the device-list card reads it (source advert: govee_manufacturer_data device_state read as power_state, on when its byte == 1; AbsBleIotItem.B -> AbsBaseBleModel.z -> BleUtil.parseBleBroadOnOff).

power_live.description: Live power after connect: 'heartbeat_aa01' = aa 01 heartbeat, on when frame byte 2 == 1 (!= 0 under the wire power light_heartbeat_nonzero or light_nonzero); 'heartbeat_aa36' = aa 36 heartbeat, per bar byte 2 / 3 == 1; 'heartbeat_aa33' = aa 33 switch heartbeat, on when byte 2 != 0; 'push_30' = the ee 30 notify (layout: wire forms.f_ee_30).

mode_color_parse.description: The family's default colour-report strategy; by_goods_type.<gt>, else by_model.<SKU>, overrides it, then that entry's by_pact and every matching by_firmware (clientBranch, clientFirmware); 'none' = no colour sub-mode decoded.

mode_color_parse_status.description: Strategy for the 0x05 TLV of the 0xAC status burst where it differs from the aa 05 reply (absent = mode_color_parse).

by_model.description: Per-SKU overrides (keys = a model of the family): the colour report and the Kelvin and brightness ranges; a by_goods_type entry for the device's gt wins over it.

by_goods_type.description: Per-goodsType rows (keys = the goodsType in decimal) that win over the family-level values; a key goods_types lacks is the goods_type of an assigned_goods_type item. A row with support is a BLE route for its models (clientRow).

relay_power.description: Plugs: what the detail screen's power button writes: 'outlet0' = 33 01 11 / 10 (relay 0), 'all_outlets' = 33 01 FF / F0, 'total_switch' = 33 02 01 / 00 (H5089) (split_plugnew/com/govee/h5080/ble/controller/).

relay_on_mask.description: Plugs: on at the connect read when (aa 01 reply byte 0 & relay_on_mask) != 0, bit i = relay i, absent = a light (govee_profile power_rule.relay_on_mask); an integer written in hex in the YAML.

advert_on_mask.description: Plugs: the device list reads on when (Govee AD switch byte & advert_on_mask) != 0 (govee_profile power_rule.advert_on_mask: govee_manufacturer_data device_state read as govee_state power_state, source advert); an integer written in hex in the YAML.

wire_cipher.description: Always 'runtime': the cipher is resolved per connection from the advert encrypted bit / BGC info, never per SKU.

sources.description: Decompiled file:line citations backing this entry.

assignedGoodsType.description: One goodsType the app assigns some of a family's SKUs itself.

context.description: 'device_list' = the device-list click handler opens the control screen with goods_type; 'bind' = the pairing flow writes goods_type (and pact) into the account record it creates.

models.description: The family's SKUs the rule covers.

from_goods_type.description: device_list only: record goodsTypes whose route reaches the rewriting click handler (0 for a SKU-keyed one).

pact.description: bind only (required there): the 'pactType,pactCode' (decimal) written with goods_type, which is also the one advertised pact the write is made at (the rule compares the advert's pact with exactly this pair: NewRgb2TLUtil.isNewRgb2TL / isNewRgb2TL4BleIot), so the item says nothing about the SKUs at any other pact. A row of another goodsType that lists one of its SKUs must not accept this pact (nor any), and no row that lists one is a route for an advertisement without a pact: the app runs other facts at this pact than at the row's (H615A-E: Config.Zv / Config.aw, Support4StringLightV2.b), and a client without the pact can't tell which applies.

rule.description: The app predicate (com.govee.base2home.pact.support) that decides it; condition restates it on the record.

doc.description: Where the app does it (path:line relative to decomp-7.7.02).

assignedGoodsTypeCondition.description: Tests on the device record, all of which must hold: pactType >= min_pact_type and pactCode >= min_pact_code separately, versions as one integer with the dots dropped (BleUtil.parseVersion; empty or unparsable = 0, fails).

min_soft_version.description: Minimum BLE firmware (soft) version of the record.

min_hard_version.description: Minimum BLE hardware version of the record.

modeColorParse.description: A colour-report strategy name (a key of the top-level mode_color_parse); 'none' = no colour sub-mode decoded, 'untraced' = the screen's code is not in the capture.

modeColorDecodeKind.description: A colour mode-report body decode name: a key of mode_color_decode, a govee_common::color_decode member other than not_decoded.

modeColorVersion.description: A firmware version 'a.bb.cc', compared field by field; an empty or unparsable device version fails (the older branch applies).

commandId.description: A govee_common::command member id (govee_common.ksy enum command), e.g. cmd_41, color_group, plug_sync_time.

anyOf.description: An aa <command> read, by its govee_common::command id.

The 0xAC special-info read ac a1 (govee_ble_frame.ksy status_command special_info), whose reply's segment IC record (sub segment_ic, govee_status_stream segment_ic_info) is the device's segment count: the goodsType 180 screen's (VM4Light.x5).

docRef.description: Citations in the .ksy doc-ref form (spec/checks/lint.py REF_FILE / REF_ADDR): a decompiled file's path:line relative to decomp-7.7.02, or IMAGE symbol @0xaddr. A path under govee-apk-decompiled/sources/ is a Govee Home 7.5.12 (1088) path, used where the 7.7.02 capture lacks the code (the h604a rows, whose 7.7.02 module pact_h604a is not captured); the row's doc says so.

clientRow.description: One goodsType row of client_profile.by_goods_type. Its fields override the family-level ones. A row with support is a BLE route: a client that knows the SKU and the advertised pact picks the rows whose models list the SKU, whose connectivity (else the family's) holds ble and whose pacts hold the pact (or are 'any'); the row then carries every fact a client needs to drive it (allOf below). The layered facts (scene_versions, kelvin_range, brightness_range) resolve on the row (its own values, then by_pact, then every matching by_firmware), else from the family specs.

models.description: The family's SKUs at this goodsType (a subset of models): the SKUs routed to this row, as traced; the app may serve others at this goodsType.

connectivity.description: This goodsType's links where they differ from the family's; a row without ble is never a BLE route.

pacts.description: The 'pactType,pactCode' pairs (decimal) the app accepts for this goodsType (Support.addSupportPact); 'any' where the route tests no pact (a goodsType-0 SKU match). A row without pacts is never a route. On a row that a pact-conditioned assigned_goods_type item reassigns its SKUs to, only the pairs at or above its gate, and such a row is never a route for an advertisement without a pact (the app rewrites only a record whose pact meets the gate); on a row of a goodsType it reassigns from, only pairs below it. A row that lists a SKU a bind item names is never a route for an advertisement without a pact either (the item's pact).

pact_required.description: The row is a route only for an advertisement that carries a pact, as a pact-conditioned reassignment's target row and a row that lists a SKU a bind item names are (pacts above): the app accepts other pacts for this goodsType that run a path this row doesn't serve, so a unit advertising none may be one of them. The row's doc names those pacts and their path. Never on a row whose pacts are 'any'.

support.description: The row's evidence. app_traced = the row's facts traced on the control-screen path and cited in doc-ref (a gap the trace knows of is named in doc), or, on a session: per_command row, on the device-list card's path, where the control screen has no BLE control (doc names the decision); hardware_verified = app_traced, and the control path also observed on a device (doc names the device, the date and what was seen); modelled = inferred, not traced, or traced but held because the library does not yet send what the app sends (doc names the gap); admitted only on the client's opt-in.

session.description: How the app's path holds the BLE link (absent = held). 'held' = the control screen's: one link across commands and reads, each write acked, the row's heartbeat running. 'per_command' = the device-list card's (timing.per_command; CardCommManagerProxy.comm2Device -> u -> triggerBleCmd$2): each command opens its own link, set up as every link is (the BGC read, the handshake where the advert or BGC says so), writes its one frame with no reply wait, then closes, and links to one address are at least timing.per_command.gap_ms apart.

oneOf.description: No keep-alive: the path holds no link between commands (session per_command); the card builds its client with a null heart message (ClientUnionFactory.buildBleMgr), and the heart loop returns on it (BleClientProxy funcRealTimeLoop).

heartbeat.description: The keep-alive read the control screen sends while the link is up (timing.heartbeat): aa <command> with the zero fill, govee_ble_frame read_request with no selector. The command is a govee_common::command member id: the ConnectHeartbeat type the screen's view model picks, ShareVM.K3 = ConnectHeartbeat.a(I3()): 1 power = aa 01 when I3 is true, 2 heartbeat = aa 00 when it is false (ConnectHeartbeat.c also maps 3 -> aa 33 and 4 -> aa 36); or the controller of the IHeart its A3 sets (BleComm.l: aa 36 on H6047 / H6042, aa 33 on H610A); or the plug screens' (h5080 BleComm.l HeartControllerV2, ctlchannel HeartGMessage: aa 01); or 'none' where the path sends none. Set on each row with support, which cites the deciding Class.method in doc-ref; no family default.

heartbeat_timing.description: When the heartbeat goes out (timing.heartbeat.timing): 'fixed_rate' = every interval_ms from the screen's start (AbsBle.HeartRunnable; a tick due while the link is busy is dropped, not queued); 'after_quiet' = interval_ms after the last frame the screen sent, every send restarting the wait (ctlchannel HeartHandler.e). Absent = fixed_rate.

heartbeat_power.description: true = the library follows the screen's aa 01 keep-alive power on this status row (timing.heartbeat.deviations; DeviceProfile.heartbeat_power): the 0xAC status read once per link, as the screen reads it once per connect (afterConnectedSingleReadDeviceInfo), then the power from byte 2 == 1 of each aa 01 reply (BleComm.G -> ShareVM.N3 -> J3). Only on a status row (power_read ac_status) whose power_live has heartbeat_aa01, with heartbeat power and no zones (the reply is the one switch). An opt-in, not a fact the app adds: every status row on the aa 01 keep-alive has that screen behaviour. Absent = the status read on every poll, its TLV 0x01 standing in for the reply, as on every status row admitted before 1.9.0.

white_type.description: The slot of the h60a6 scheme's colour-temperature frame (govee_ble_frame op15_color, form kelvin_tint): the white type the colour page hands Bytes.r, the app's ColorTemperatureType as LightColorCapabilityCenter.d1 gives it (Config.H: Config.O by SKU, else Config.P by goodsType, else 1) on the path the screen runs (ColorModeControllerConfig.c -> Config.Yt). rgb_white (1) = ff ff ff; rgb_black (0) = 00 00 00; rgb_self_tem_color (3) = 00 00 00 over a whole posSet and, over a partial one, the tint in the slot with Kelvin and tint zero. Absent = rgb_white. Not Config.P read raw: a screen whose colour page passes its own value takes that (the rgbiclight ColorControllerConfig passes 1, so goodsType 176, Config.P 0, is rgb_white), and RGB_SELF (2) builds as rgb_white in Bytes.r. The illumination tab's Kelvin (Config.N -> Bytes.C) tests rgb_black alone, so its slot can differ (rgb_self_tem_color leads ff ff ff there). Only on an h60a6 row.

color_temp_control.description: Where and how the control screen sets colour temperature when it isn't the colour page's one-frame Kelvin over the pieces selected: whole_device = that one-frame write, but always over every piece (the screen's canClickColorTem returns an all-true posSet whatever is selected, e.g. h61d3 ColorMode.canClickColorTem on 239 / 246, H61D3Support.i0), so the screen has no Kelvin on part of the device and the library refuses one (DeviceProfile.whole_device_kelvin); illumination = the illumination tab alone (the colour page, if any, has no Kelvin), which sends the Kelvin frame and then 33 04 <the current brightness> as one write (View4IlluminationMode.I0: KelvinConfig.b -> ColorModeControllerConfig.h -> Config.N[Config.x], then BrightnessConfig.b of illuminationCur()[0], one Compose4DefWrite). The row's color_scheme is the one whose colour-temperature frame is that Config.N builder (h60a6 = Bytes.C, h6188 = Bytes.A, kelvin_v9 = Bytes.D), and its brightness is percent; the tab writes every piece, so it is whole-device too. Absent = the one-frame colour-temperature write (the colour page's Kelvin, over the selected pieces where the row has segments), on every row before 1.8.0.

power_index.description: The zone's index in its power write (33 30 <index>; 33 36 bar order).

segments.description: The colour pieces (mask bits) the zone covers.

account_lock.description: The control screen sends the 0xB2 secret check after the handshake on every connect, and the device ignores commands until it does. The family encryption tag secret_key_pairing describes the pairing / group flows, not this.

scene_dialect.description: How the control screen uploads a scene: a key of scenes.upload.dialects (legacy_scene = ScenesOp.parseSceneV1 for every sceneType, also on a goodsType that registers a new-DIY parser, where BaseSceneViewMode.r3 first takes a sceneType-5 scene whose param leads 0x50; the library uploads no sceneType-5 scene under legacy_scene, so a legacy_scene SKU's bundled catalog holds none that the app uploads: none leading 0x50, and none at all where the scene versions hold a sceneType-5 branch of parseSceneV1 (7 to 13; tools/fetch_scenes.py leaves them out); diy_graffiti / tablelamp_h6052_type5_diy = that dialect for sceneType 5, parseSceneV1 for the rest), 'none' = activate only, 'untraced' = the apply path is not traced.

kelvin_range.description: [min, max] CCT in kelvin of this goodsType's colour page; wins over the family's specs.kelvin_range.

mode_reports_kelvin.description: false = the device's aa 05 colour report carries Kelvin 0 after a colour-temperature write, so the Kelvin last written stands, as the screen keeps what it set (hardware-observed; doc names the device); absent = the report carries it.

kelvin_readback.description: Where the screen takes the colour-temperature state from on a read-back, where not the mode report's Kelvin (absent). pieces = the colour read-back's pieces, once the connect read has read them all: the Kelvin of their one colour when every piece shows the same one and it is one of the app's tint colours (its whole 1000-10000 K table, ColorUtils.C, not the row's kelvin_range), else none; it replaces the mode report's Kelvin as the colour mode's, and a non-zero one is the screen's held Kelvin whatever the mode (goodsType 180: VM4Light.g5 -> ColorUtils.r, SubMode4Color.s, syncKelvin). Needs color_temp and the direct colour read-back on a polled row whose walk is not IC-sized.

status_read.description: The connect read is the 0xAC status read (no aa 01 / aa 05 reads): the types it requests (govee_ble_frame status_read_args.types), in request order; [] = the bare read ac 03 00, no types requested, whose reply carries the TLVs the firmware chooses (Compose4BaseInfoSingleRead.Companion.a passes no ext bytes; the h70dx screen); absent = no status read.

connect_reads.description: The state reads the control screen sends at connect besides the power read (power_read / relay_on_mask) and the aa 05 mode read (mode_color_parse), in the app's order: aa <command> reads and the 0xAC special-info read (connectRead); device-info, timer and Wi-Fi reads are not listed. On a status_read row they are the reads sent before the 0xAC read, in the same connect read (Compose4BaseInfoSingleRead.Companion.c adds them ahead of its time sync and ControllerSingleRead), each one a mandatory step of it (AbsComposeControllerWithOpResult.onOvertime fails the read).

post_status_reads.description: On a status_read row: the state reads (aa <command>) the screen sends after the 0xAC read succeeds, in the app's order (h7020 NewDetailVM$afterConnectedSingleReadDeviceInfo4702ABC$1.o -> NewDetailVM.s5), the setting reads left out as in connect_reads; absent = none.

connect_writes.description: The writes sent on every connect after the handshake and any account_lock check, in order.

power_resync.description: Plugs: after each acked power write the screen re-runs its connect sequence (device-info reads, connect_writes).

rounding.description: How the division rounds: ceil (absent: IC / n + (IC % n != 0), H61D3Support.e) or floor (Java's integer division IC / n, h705a Support.b for 125 / 240).

skip_zero.description: true = an IC count of 0 gives no count, as a failed read: the screen's IC check skips it and keeps the count it stored (h705a VM4H608A.S4 for 184), so the writes keep the count they have and that poll's walk is skipped. Absent = 0 is a count.

oneOf.description: clamp(IC, min_ic, max_ic) / ic_per_piece pieces, rounded as rounding says (up when absent).

table.description: IC counts the rule names, each with its pieces (an IC at most once).

otherwise.description: The pieces at any other IC count.

oneOf.description: Pieces by the IC count's value: the entry's where the IC equals its ic, else otherwise (h6609 Support.getColorPieceSize(173, IC): 18 at 36, else 14).

pair_max.description: The most pieces each strip's IC count gives.

otherwise.description: The pieces when the reply carries no second strip.

oneOf.description: Two strips: min(IC 1, pair_max) + min(IC 2, pair_max) where the IC-pair reader (ControllerIcNum.e) returns a second pair, the first IC is not 0 (the list VM4Light.h5 keeps) and the second is above 0, else otherwise; no count where that reader throws (govee_state ic_count app_pair_fails). H61D3Support.e and ColorModeH1A45's strip for goodsType 375: min(ic1, 15) + min(ic2, 15), else 30.

The aa 40 IC count does not size the pieces: the screen reads it and the library discards it. The pieces are the row's static count, or, with the special_info connect read, the segment count the device reports (goodsType 180).

The read-back walks the aa 40 reply's two section bytes summed as Java bytes (govee_state ic_count section_sum, as the sectioned IC-pair reader ControllerIcNum.d passes them on) when the sum is not 0, else the row's static pieces, in Java's sum / group + (sum % group != 0) groups (none below 1); no walk where the reader throws (rgbiclight VM4Light.N5). Writes keep the static pieces.

ic_pieces.description: The colour pieces from the IC count read at connect: the aa 40 read (connect_reads ic_num, and on a status_read row post_status_reads ic_num: the reads around the 0xAC read) or, on a status_read row, the 0xAC read's TLV 0x40 (status_read ic_num), which the row's wire f_40 reads (one_count signed, one_count_u16 unsigned: govee_state ic_count ic_count / ic_count_u16, with no byte-order check). Each read stores the count, as the screen does (Info4BleIotDevice.G0), and a TLV 0x40 ahead of the TLV 0xA5 sizes that burst's colour groups, as the screen's lambda reads q() at each 0xA5 TLV. An object form derives the pieces from the aa 40 reply's IC count (govee_state ic_count ic_count_checked; no count where it is absent), or from its IC pair, or from the TLV 0x40's count; a status_read row takes the object forms only. Where the row's wire f_40 is ic_pair the screen reads the reply with the IC-pair reader (ControllerIcNum.e), and there is no count where that reader throws (govee_state ic_count app_pair_fails: either IC field 0x1000 or more), whichever form; the pair form needs it. An object form's pieces size the direct read-back's walk and every colour write: they are every pick's position set, the whole-device mask included, with no cap but the rule's, as the screens that size their strip by the IC count build it (ColorPieceConfig.c over the stored IC; the row's doc names its strip). A strip that the connect read does not resize (the h61d3 and H7067 screens store the count without posting deviceInfoChanged; the row's doc says so) keeps the count it was built with until a calibration or settings event, so in the first app session after the IC changed with no app connected its picks have the old count, where the library's writes take the new one. The row's wire num_segments is then only the count before the first read. sections sizes the read-back alone.

readback_pieces.description: On a status_read row with an ic_pieces object form: the status read's TLV 0xA5 colour groups are placed over the IC count itself (ic_count: the count as the row's IC read gives it, as Support.getColorPieceSize(gt, IC) = IC on the h7050 and h7020 status screens), while ic_pieces sizes the writes. Absent = the ic_pieces rule's pieces size both.

per_unit.description: The pieces per unit of the count: the bulbs per string the screen multiplies it by (h7020 NewDetailVM.Y5: Support.getBulbStringSetting [1] at the row's goodsType and pact), or 1 where the screen stores the count itself (h7020 NewDetailVM.u5 on goodsType 149).

light_num_pieces.description: The colour pieces from the aa 0f string-count read at connect (connect_reads light_num): the reply's count (govee_state light_num_state count) times per_unit, which the screen stores as its IC (h7020 NewDetailVM.u5 -> Info4BleIotDevice.G0), so the count its colour strip takes at each pick (ColorPieceConfig.c over the stored IC; the row's doc names its strip). As an ic_pieces object form's pieces, they size the direct read-back's walk and every colour write, the whole-device mask included. A count below 1 is no count: the app would size no pieces or a negative number. The row's wire num_segments is only the count before the first read. A row with support that reads light_num has this; it is the row's one live piece count (no ic_pieces object form, no aa 41 section count).

clientCapabilities.description: The controls the goodsType's control screen offers on the BLE path, by control whichever page offers it (color_functions, where traced, is the colour page's own flag set and agrees with it): gradual = the 0xA3 gradual flag, segments = per-piece colour (and segment brightness where color_functions has it, colorFunctions). The family specs and the row's layered facts give each one's range.

clientModel.description: A per-SKU override: mode_color_parse, the Kelvin and brightness ranges (used where the SKU's by_goods_type row has none), their pact and firmware branches, the scene apply's power-on, and the connect writes.

kelvin_range.description: [min, max] CCT in kelvin of this SKU's colour page (KelvinConfig by SKU); the row's own kelvin_range wins over it.

brightness_range.description: This SKU's brightness range; the row's own brightness_range wins over it.

scene_power_on.description: true = the control screen writes the power-on switch (33 01 01, SwitchControllerConfig.d) ahead of a scene or DIY apply while its stored switch state for the device is off, and an unknown state reads as off (ApplyOffNeedOpenConfig's SKU set, ApplyOffNeedOpenHelper.b / .d, DeviceSwitchConfig.getSwitch); absent = false. Only on a SKU whose row offers scenes.

connect_writes.description: This SKU's connect writes, replacing its row's, which stay required for the row's other SKUs: the screen splits them by SKU within one goodsType (bulblight Support.c at 342). Only on a SKU that one row of the family lists.

clientBranch.description: A pact branch of a client_profile row: applied over the row's own values when the device's pact is the key, its leaves replacing the row's. The pact is the advertised one where the screen scans before connecting, else the record's; with the pact unknown, the row's own values apply. Firmware branches stay on the row (by_firmware), as in wire.

clientFirmware.description: A firmware branch of a client_profile row, applied after by_pact when its every min_* holds (versions compare as modeColorVersion, but a kelvin_range item's min_hard_version or min_soft_version is a string compare, as KelvinConfig.Config.z2's versionHard.compareTo and Z2 / X2's versionSoft.compareTo are: hard 10.00.00 is below 3.08.01; an empty or unparsable device version fails). Every matching item applies, in list order, a later item's leaves replacing an earlier's: the app's version gates are independent per fact (unlike wire's by_firmware, where the first match applies). No match keeps the row's values; firmware facts resolve after the device-info read, so capabilities never depend on them.

colorFunctions.description: The colour page's segment-brightness and colour-temperature flags, the 4th and 5th of the app's five normal-function flags (color Config.e, base-classes11/com/govee/base2light/pact/newdetail/config/fuc/color/Config.java:551-560): a listed name is on, an unlisted one off; absent = not traced. segment_brightness = the relative-brightness slider (its frame is the family's segment_brightness_write); color_temperature = the Kelvin slider over kelvin_range (the colour write's CCT form). The library sends segment brightness (33 05 15 02) on a row with segments only where segment_brightness is listed, or color_functions is absent (the 1.x rule), and the colour scheme has that frame (h60a6); listed without segments on such a scheme is refused.

sub_modes.description: Colour sub-mode byte -> the mode_color_decode kind applied to its body ('0x14' only where a package uses it as its colour sub-mode); empty = none decoded.

layout.description: Bytes read after the sub-mode byte (body offsets, sizes, endianness).

kelvin_signed.description: true = Kelvin read signed (0x8000-0xFFFF negative); false = unsigned; null = no Kelvin read.

cct_rule.description: When the screen shows the report as a colour temperature vs an RGB colour.

wire.description: The device's govee_profile context (spec/govee_profile.ksy) as data, layered this block, by_model.<SKU>, by_goods_type.<gt> (each: own fields, by_pact, first matching by_firmware), a later layer replacing single leaves and an unset leaf being the param's 0.

mode_status.description: The 0xAC TLV 0x05 decode, where it differs; unset leaves are mode's.

by_pact.description: Keyed 'pactType,pactCode' (decimal): applied after the layer's own fields when the device's pact matches.

by_firmware.description: Applied after by_pact: the first item whose every min_* holds (versions compare as modeColorVersion).

by_goods_type.description: Per goodsType gt (a key of goods_types or client_profile.by_goods_type).

by_model.description: Per SKU (a model of the family); a by_goods_type entry wins over it.

mode_status.description: The 0xAC TLV 0x05 decode, where it differs; unset leaves are mode's.

by_pact.description: Keyed 'pactType,pactCode' (decimal): applied after the layer's own fields when the device's pact matches.

by_firmware.description: Applied after by_pact: the first item whose every min_* holds (versions compare as modeColorVersion).

wireBranch.description: A pact branch of a wire layer.

mode_status.description: The 0xAC TLV 0x05 decode, where it differs; unset leaves are mode's.

wireFirmware.description: A firmware branch of a wire layer.

mode_status.description: The 0xAC TLV 0x05 decode, where it differs; unset leaves are mode's.

wireForms.description: command_forms selectors by member name; an absent selector is unknown (0).

wireCounts.description: device_counts: the static defaults; a count the device reports at runtime (aa 40 / aa 41 / TLV 0x40) replaces them.

num_segments.description: posSet length of the write mask (seg_mask.num_segments).

wirePower.description: power_rule without relay_on_mask and advert_on_mask (those are the by_goods_type entry's).

relay_heartbeat_on_mask.description: aa 01 heartbeat: on when (byte & mask) != 0, 0 = as relay_on_mask; written in hex in the YAML.

light_nonzero.description: A light's aa 01 connect read is on at any non-zero byte, as the screen's decoder reads it (the legacy SwitchController, the H70BX connect read); absent or false = on at == 1 (ControllerSwitch.Companion.c).

light_heartbeat_nonzero.description: A light's aa 01 heartbeat is on at any non-zero byte where its connect read is on at == 1 (H1168: HeartControllerWithBattery, Compose4ReadAllInfo); absent or false = as light_nonzero. The library's poll follows the heartbeat rule, as with relay_heartbeat_on_mask.

wireMode.description: mode_decode without the colour kinds (those are the resolved mode_color_parse / mode_color_parse_status sub_modes).

timing.description: Connection + command timing constants (milliseconds unless noted).

heartbeat.description: The keep-alive read the control screens send while the link is up; each row with support names its command (clientRow heartbeat) and timing (clientRow heartbeat_timing).

interval_ms.description: The beat period, and the after_quiet wait (AbsBle.F; BleClientProxy.Builder f).

timing.description: The two mechanisms, one per heartbeat_timing value.

skip.description: When a due tick sends nothing.

reply.description: What the screen does with the reply.

failure.description: How a beat is written, and what its failure does.

firmware.description: FIRMWARE-SOURCED: what the device does without it.

deviations.description: PROCEDURAL: where a client of this spec (govee-ble-local) differs from the app, each a decision.

per_command.description: The device-list card's BLE session (clientRow session per_command): one link per command.

gap_ms.description: The least time between one session's release and the next session's start to the same address (CardCommManagerProxy.s).

command_timeout_ms.description: The card's bound on one command, its BLE and IoT legs together (CardCommManagerProxy.r).

client.description: The client the card builds for a session, and its link setup.

send.description: How the session's one frame goes out, and what counts as success.

deviations.description: PROCEDURAL: where a client of this spec (govee-ble-local) differs from the card, each a decision.
